First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{24}$ into the above, we get

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{24})
$$

which simplifies as

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})
$$

Now, we can rewrite the given expression using the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})}{\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})} & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})}{\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the double-angle formula once more with $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$, we can further simplify the above expression: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})}{\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})} & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
